title: Briefing: Canada's Pacific Link pipeline, Italy's protest decree, and the Cockroach Janta Party
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Wednesday, October twenty-first. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

Canada has designated a new oil pipeline from Alberta to British Columbia, called Pacific Link, as its first fast-tracked national project. Cold Lake First Nations has gone to federal court to quash that designation, saying it was not consulted; that's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: British Columbia's election on October twenty-fourth, and a First Nations meeting on October twenty-sixth.

Students and cost-of-living protesters have been marching against Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government after clashes with police in Milan. Italy's Council of Ministers has approved a decree sending five hundred soldiers to Milan, without arrest powers; that's confirmed by independent reports. Accounts differ on whether it extends preventive detention to minors: Il Post says yes, Il Fatto Quotidiano says no. What's next: the decree's final text, and the general strike unions have called for November twentieth.

The Cockroach Janta Party movement began in India as a satirical response to a judge's remark about unemployed youth, and now wants the chief election commissioner to resign over a disputed voter-roll revision. The movement has asked the Delhi High Court to free two detained spokespeople, arguing their custody violates their right to liberty; that's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: an October twenty-first sureties hearing, and that High Court petition's outcome.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
